name: motion
description: 캔버스 코드로 굽는 2D 모션그래픽·캐릭터 애니메이션 영상 — 씬 선언(JSON)을 받아 쇼츠 mp4, 정지 스틸, 투명 클립아트 스티커 PNG 를 만든다. 배경은 그라디언트·밤하늘·image_gen 실사 이미지, 위에 캐릭터(파이어뱃)·말풍선·타이틀·정보카드·라인업·불꽃놀이·하트·켄번즈 이미지 층을 얹는다. BGM·음성 트랙 먹싱과 음성 립싱크 지원.

settings_fields.label: 한글 폰트 경로
settings_fields.description: 텍스트 렌더에 쓸 TTF/TTC 경로입니다. 비워 두면 시스템에서 나눔고딕·Noto CJK·맑은고딕 순으로 찾습니다. 한글 폰트가 없으면 한글이 든 씬은 명시 에러로 거부됩니다 (Debian/Ubuntu: apt install fonts-nanum).

actions.name: 영상 렌더
actions.description: 씬 선언을 mp4 로 굽는다 — 캐릭터·텍스트·불꽃·이미지 층을 타임라인에 얹고, BGM·음성을 먹싱한다. stills 를 주면 영상 대신 지정 시각의 정지 PNG 만 뽑는다(수정 반복용 싼 검수 경로). 씬 문법·에셋 목록은 assets 액션이 전부 말한다.

actions.name: 클립아트 스티커
actions.description: 클립아트를 투명 배경 PNG 로 내보낸다 — 캐릭터(포즈 지정)·하트·별·달·말풍선(문구 옵션)을 페이지·문서·PPT 에서 재사용한다.

actions.name: 클립아트 저장
actions.description: 캐릭터·소품을 재사용하게 저장한다 — 선언(JSON)이 원본으로 남고 썸네일 PNG 가 미디어 창고(클립아트 칩)에 뜬다. 두 형태 중 하나다: 도형 파츠 리그(parts), 또는 동작마다 한 장씩 그려진 애니메이션 시트(sheets — 걷기·절·날기 같은 프레임 그림). 저장 후엔 씬 sprite 와 sticker 가 이름으로 참조한다. 문법은 assets 액션이 말한다.

actions.name: 클립아트 삭제
actions.description: 저장된 클립아트 선언을 지운다. 미디어 창고의 썸네일은 창고에서 따로 지운다.

actions.name: 영상 자르기
actions.desc: Cut or split an existing mp4 by seconds with ffmpeg stream copy — no re-render. {media, from?, to} or {media, segments:[{from,to}..6]}.

actions.name: 3D 모델 정보
actions.desc: Inspect a rigged .glb: clip names and durations, triangle count, height. Call before using a model3d scene layer.

actions.name: 오디오 길이
actions.description: 미디어 창고 오디오 파일의 길이(초)를 잰다 — 대사(voices)와 말풍선·talk 액트를 타임라인에 배치하기 전에 줄마다 부른다.

actions.name: 렌더 잡 상태
actions.description: async:true 로 접수한 렌더의 진행률을 조회한다 — 돌고 있으면 진행률·남은 시간, 끝났으면 그 응답으로 영상을 미디어 창고에 반입한다.

actions.name: 에셋·씬 문법 사전
actions.description: 이 모듈이 그릴 수 있는 것 전부 — 레이어 종류별 필드, 캐릭터 포즈 파라미터, 배경 종류, 캡·기본값. render 를 부르기 전에 여기부터 읽는다.

actions.name: 셀프테스트
actions.description: Offline regression checks — frame geometry, sprite pixel floor, sticker alpha, scene math, tiny encode, font resolution. 자체 검사

action.description: Which capability to run. Call assets first for the full scene grammar.

duration.description: [render] Video length in seconds, 0.5 to 90. Over ~30s prefer draft quality; a long story can also ship as several clips.

background.description: [render] Background layer. {kind:'night'} = built-in starry night with moon and hills (default). {kind:'studio'} = bright presenter stage with spotlight and floor — made for caster/info videos. {kind:'gradient', top:[r,g,b], bottom:[r,g,b]}. {kind:'image', media:'/user/media/....png'} = a generated or stored image, cover-cropped — pair with image_gen for photoreal backdrops. All take vignette: 0..0.6 edge darkening (0 disables).

layers.description: [render] Scene layers drawn in order, each with from/to seconds. Kinds: sprite (a saved or seed character by `name`; a character saved with drawn sheets plays them with plays:[{action, at, for?, travel?}] — pose/wave/anim acts do not apply to drawn frames, but a move act carries it across the screen, which is how anything that does not walk (a bird, a ball) travels; a grounded sheet also gets a soft contact shadow under its feet, as wide as the feet are in that frame — shadow:false turns it off, a number 0..1 dims it; a shape/cutout rig takes enter walk/peek/pop, acts wave/talk/jump/point/pose/anim/move (move eases position to:[x,y] and holds — chain for paths) — anim plays hand-keyed 2D cartoon keypose cycles walk/run/idle/punch/dance (prefer over mocap clip for cartoon rigs), pose takes ease snap/overshoot/anticipate and squash — point taps a normalized [x,y] target with a presenter stick, pose keyframes declared bones — and clip: built-in CMU mocap walk/punch/boxing/dance or any BVH from the media store driving the bones), bubble (speech balloon, typing), title (stacked display lines), caption (subtitle pill), card (label/value info rows), list (time-table rows with color dots and a highlight tag), image (media picture with optional Ken Burns pan-zoom), spritesheet (animated frame-grid image: media+grid:[cols,rows]+fps, loops — free game sprite sheets work as-is), fireworks, hearts, confetti, spark (impact flash), shake (camera shake), speedlines, hpbar (fighting-game health bar), model3d (a rigged 3D character .glb toon-rendered server-side — built-in robot with 13 clips or any media-store glb; clip/plays picks animations, model_info lists them). Field-level contract comes from the assets action.

audio.description: [render] Optional sound: {bgm, voice, voices:[{media, at}], bgmGainDb:-8}. voice = one file at t=0; voices places dialogue lines on the timeline (measure each with the duration action, then align bubble/talk windows to the same at). Voice ducks the bgm and its envelope drives the mouth of sprites whose talk act has lipsync — mouth sync is automatic.

stills.description: [render] Timestamps in seconds. When present, exports still PNGs at these times INSTEAD of a video — seconds instead of minutes, use it to iterate on a scene before the final render.

quality.description: [render] 'final' (default, 1.5x supersampled) or 'draft' (1x, roughly twice as fast) for quick previews.

name.description: [sticker|save_asset|delete_asset] Asset name. sticker exports any clip-art declaration — the seeds shipped with the module (firebat, heart, star, moon, balloon) or one saved with save_asset; save_asset names the new declaration (1-24 chars, letters/digits/한글/-/_).

media.description: [duration|trim] Media-store path (/user/media/...) — duration: an audio file, trim: an mp4.

segments.description: [trim] Up to 6 {from,to} spans — each becomes its own file.

camera.description: [render] Scene zoom/pan keyframes [{at, zoom:1..4, center:[x,y], in?}] — eases from the previous state and holds; the way to zoom into a spot while it is being talked about (never swap background images per segment).

async.description: [render] true = validate, return a jobId immediately, and render in the background — REQUIRED for renders longer than ~20s (they outlive the tool roundtrip). Poll with the job action; the poll that sees it finished imports the video.

id.description: [job] jobId returned by render with async:true.

redeliver.description: [job] Re-import a finished video that was already delivered once (default false).

bones.description: [save_asset] Optional FK bone chains {name: {pivot:[x,y], parent?}} (max 40). Parts tagged bone:'name' follow their bone; children follow parents (shoulder->elbow->fist). Drive with the pose act {do:'pose', bones:{name:degrees}} or sticker pose.bones.

parts.description: [save_asset] The clip art's shape parts — the ORIGINAL that scenes and stickers redraw from. 100x100 viewBox, feet at (50,100), y down. Each part: {shape: ellipse|rect|polygon|capsule|heart|star, at/size or points or ends+width, fill:[r,g,b], outline?, role: swing (waves) | mouth (opens on talk) | eye (blinks)}. shape 'image' = cutout rigging: {media, crop polygon in 0..1 image coords, at, width, pivot?, role?} turns a piece of an attached picture into a joint. Full grammar: the assets action. Alternative to sheets — a drawn character needs no parts.

sheets.description: [save_asset] A character whose actions are DRAWN frames instead of a posed rig: {<action name>: {media, fps?, loop?, frames?, anchor?}} — media is one sheet path, or a LIST of sheets for an action too long to fit on one canvas (a dozen full-height figures come back with the bottom row's feet cut off; ask for 6 frames a sheet and list four of them). Frames are numbered straight through the list. Ask image_gen for: one action split into N distinct frames with the wing/limb position named for EACH frame and no two alike (asking for "8 frames" alone comes back as three drawings and five near-copies); the body held still so only the moving part moves; and a TRANSPARENT background, adding that if transparency is not possible it should use a flat solid backdrop of one stated colour (e.g. magenta #FF00FF) that appears NOWHERE on the character, since that colour is keyed out on import and any of it in the drawing is a hole. Stating the colour is followed closely — measured, #FF00FF came back as rgb(247,5,245) over 99.8% of the ground; saying only "transparent" came back three different ways (real alpha, green, a painted checkerboard). frame boxes are read off the image, so no coordinates are typed, and cells that came back within 15% of each other in height are put on one size -- that scatter is the generator drawing one character at different sizes, and left in it reads as his height dropping mid-stride; past 15% the difference is taken as the action (a raised wing, a crouch) and the drawings are left alone. frames is the play order, counting the drawings off the sheet from 1 (one number = a held pose, which is how `idle` and `walk` come off the SAME sheets: idle takes the standing frame, walk takes the cycle and leaves it out) — a generated sheet is not always a cycle, and [1,2,3,2] turns three drawings into a beat that loops, drops a bad frame, or holds one twice. A backdrop of one flat colour is keyed out on import, so a chroma-key sheet works too. Scenes play it as {kind:'sprite', name, plays:[{action, at, for?, travel?:'right'|'left'}]} — travel walks at the sheet's own measured stride, which is what stops a walker from skating; a sheet whose feet never separate (a bird, a bow) has no stride, so move it with a move act instead. fps is the animation cadence, not the video's (8 = anime's 3s, 12 = 2s), and travel advances on THAT beat rather than the video's, so the walker steps forward once per drawing: sliding a sprite under a picture that is being held drags its planted foot along and snaps it back when the next drawing lands, which measured 44px eight times a second on the shipped walk (2026-09-01, 9.4% of the figure's height). One cycle of the frames list always covers one cycle of ground, so a frames list that repeats a drawing ([1,2,3,4,5,6,3,7] = eight frames off seven drawings) does not walk faster than the seven. face -- {} or {from: N, bottom?: 0.08..0.6} -- puts ONE head on every frame: the bank head (the biggest on the sheet, or drawing N) is pasted over each frame's own at draw time, erase-then-paste, so the face the generator redraws differently every call becomes literally the same pixels in every frame (measured 2026-09-01: seven rendered frames identical to 0.0%, unbanked 4.2%). For actions where only the head crosses the neck line -- a walk, a bow; not a wave. anchor says what `at` pins: 'feet' (default) puts every frame's bottom on one line, which is what standing on the ground means; 'body' pins whatever every frame of the action has in common — overlay them and the part that lands on itself is the character, the rest is the motion — and is what an airborne action needs — a flying bird's frame is as tall as its raised wing, so aligning bottoms swings the whole bird up and down once per cycle. Alternative to parts. Full grammar: the assets action. WALK CYCLES, measured 2026-08-31. Ask for ONE frame per call, not a grid — a grid obeys cell count and figure size but not which pose goes in which cell. Angles are obeyed to about 8 degrees and pixel coordinates are ignored entirely, but two poses closer than ~10 degrees come back as the same drawing, which is why eight frames is the ceiling and twelve returns duplicates. What is obeyed best is a NAMED state (contact / weight-bearing / passing / lift-off), not a number. WHICH LEG LEADS CANNOT BE ASKED FOR. Naming the leg, calling it the opposite of the reference, saying which one is nearer the viewer, saying which one is drawn on top, and drawing it from a turnaround while spelling out that the far leg is the one striding — five ways, all answered with the near leg leading, which is simply what this generator draws. Only the reference moves it, and only if the reference ALREADY SHOWS that leg leading: a neutral reference (a turnaround, a standing pose) has no leading leg to copy and returns the default. So each half of the cycle needs its own reference and that reference has to be a walk frame, not a view. The first far-leg-forward frame is not asked for, it is FOUND — ask for a many-frame sheet with no instruction about legs and some cells come back with the other leg leading (3 of 12, measured); cut one out and it anchors that half from then on. Two anchors per character, found once. Seven drawings make eight frames: contact, weight-bearing, passing, lift-off for each half with one passing shared, played [1,2,3,4,5,6,3,7]. The two drawings either side of full stride must differ, or the motion visibly reverses there.

pose.description: [sticker] Asset parameters. firebat: {wave:0..1, mouth:0..1, blink:0..1, squash:0.7..1.3, look:[x,y]}. heart/star/moon: {color:[r,g,b]}. balloon: {text}. Omit for defaults.
